title: How To Ease The Strain On Your Students’ Mental Health
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Observing that lockdown has stripped students of social connection and control over their own lives, Linsin recommends offering more choice within the boundaries of an existing classroom management plan as a simple way to restore students' sense of autonomy and self-worth. He lists concrete categories where choice can be introduced with little added teacher effort, including writing prompts, project types, read-alouds, problem-solving methods, and submission timing, while cautioning against offering too many options at once, which can cause indecision. He frames this as newly urgent given data he cites showing a third of Americans exhibiting signs of clinical anxiety or depression, arguing that small, previously unremarkable gestures like choice now carry outsized psychological weight.
points: Offering students choice restores a sense of autonomy and self-worth stripped away by pandemic isolation.
Choices must still be offered within the boundaries of an existing classroom management plan, not as free-for-alls.
Offering too many options at once can backfire, causing students to freeze up and become indecisive.
Practical low-effort choice categories include writing prompts, project types, problem-solving methods, and submission timing.
With roughly a third of Americans showing signs of clinical anxiety or depression, small autonomy-restoring gestures now carry outsized weight.
quotes: You see, when children have limited choices in their life, as they do now, they begin to lack a sense of their own value and worth—two areas that are being pummeled by social distancing mandates.

Choices, of course, must be given within the boundaries of your classroom management plan. You also have to be careful about giving too many, as this can cause them to freeze up and become indecisive.
With one-third of all Americans showing signs of clinical anxiety and depression, many previously and barely noticeable areas of our lives have now grown into critical importance.
Something taken for granted can explode into a necessity or in its absence become a strain on our mental health.
It can give students some personal power and control at a time when they have very little of either.
